dedupe_keys.name: gis based real time risk analysis and selective evacuation for chlorine leaks near the ulsan industrial cluster south korea 2019

description: This case study develops a real-time risk analysis tool based on a geographic information system to plan emergency response and risk communication for leaks of hazardous chemicals, and applies it to a chlorine gas release near eleven buildings in Ulsan, a densely populated South Korean city next to a large industrial cluster. An assessment module weighs indoor and outdoor concentrations in each building and the release duration against the maximum allowable concentration, so that residents are told either to shelter indoors or to evacuate. In the simulation only four buildings were reached by the gas, depending on wind direction and diffusion time, and a selective indoor and outdoor plan was found more effective than evacuating everyone outdoors. It was written by Byungtae Yoo and Sang D. Choi and published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health on 1 June 2019. Coverage is one city district. The article is available free online under CC BY 4.0; the tool itself is not released. Caveats: it is a simulation for a single release scenario and a small set of buildings, with no validation against a real incident. For simulation it shows how dispersion outputs can be turned into building-level shelter or evacuate decisions for chemical plants next to housing. It is related to the CHEMM chemical incident response case studies record in this catalogue.
